title: Energy, Work and Power Module 1 Lesson 2: Raising Hauling Against Gravity Resistance custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A crane raises a load of mass $240\text{ kg}$ vertically through a height of $15\text{ m}$ at a constant speed. Assuming air resistance is negligible, calculate the work done by the crane in raising the load. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A bucket of cement of mass $35\text{ kg}$ is hoisted vertically upwards through $12\text{ m}$ at constant speed against a constant resistance to motion of $25\text{ N}$. Calculate the total work done by the hoisting cable. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A cart of mass $60\text{ kg}$ is hauled a distance of $20\text{ m}$ up a smooth plane inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal at a constant speed by a cable parallel to the line of greatest slope. Calculate the work done by the tension in the cable. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A block is pulled a distance of $16\text{ m}$ up a line of greatest slope of a rough inclined plane against a constant frictional force of $32\text{ N}$. Calculate the work done against friction during this movement.

A load of mass $40\text{ kg}$ is hauled up a line of greatest slope of a rough plane inclined at $18^\circ$ to the horizontal at a constant speed. The pulling force acts parallel to the slope and the frictional resistance opposing motion is $50\text{ N}$. Calculate the magnitude of the pulling force. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

A crate of mass $50\text{ kg}$ is lowered vertically downwards through a depth of $8\text{ m}$ by a cable exerting a constant upward tension of $420\text{ N}$. Calculate the work done by gravity, and calculate the work done by the tension in the cable. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

questions.prompt: A box of mass $20\text{ kg}$ is pulled a distance of $25\text{ m}$ up a rough plane inclined at $15^\circ$ to the horizontal at a constant speed. The box moves along a line of greatest slope against a constant frictional resistance of $35\text{ N}$. The pulling force acts parallel to the line of greatest slope. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the work done against friction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the change in gravitational potential energy of the box.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the work done by the pulling force.

questions.prompt: A mine cart of mass $350\text{ kg}$ is hauled up an inclined track of length $60\text{ m}$ from the bottom of an open-cast pit. The track is inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\alpha = \frac{5}{13}$ and $\cos\alpha = \frac{12}{13}$. A constant resistance of magnitude $180\text{ N}$ opposes the motion of the cart. The hauling cable acts parallel to the track and hauls the cart at a constant speed. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the vertical height gained by the mine cart, and calculate the increase in gravitational potential energy.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the work done against the resistance force, and determine the total work done by the winch.

questions.prompt: A winch pulls a container of mass $80\text{ kg}$ a distance of $30\text{ m}$ up a rough inclined plane at a constant speed of $1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The plane is inclined at $20^\circ$ to the horizontal, and the coefficient of friction between the container and the plane is $\mu = 0.22$. The cable of the winch is parallel to the line of greatest slope. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the normal contact force on the container and the work done against friction over the $30\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the cable, and find the rate at which the winch is doing work in watts.

questions.prompt: A service lift of mass $600\text{ kg}$ carries a passenger of mass $80\text{ kg}$. The lift is raised vertically from the ground floor to the fourth floor, through a vertical distance of $16\text{ m}$, at a constant speed of $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$. A constant resistance of $450\text{ N}$ opposes the motion of the lift. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the tension in the hoisting cable, and calculate the total work done by the hoisting cable.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the time taken for the ascent, the power developed by the lift motor, and the percentage of the total work done that is dissipated against resistance.

questions.prompt: A sledge of mass $45\text{ kg}$ is hauled up a rough track inclined at $12^\circ$ to the horizontal. The hauling cable is inclined at an angle of $18^\circ$ above the line of greatest slope of the track. The sledge moves a distance of $24\text{ m}$ up the track at a constant speed. The coefficient of friction between the sledge and the track is $\mu = 0.20$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces perpendicular to the track, show that the normal contact force is given by $R = 450\cos 12^\circ - T\sin 18^\circ$, and formulate an equation for the tension $T$ along the track.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the tension $T$ in the cable, and find the work done by the tension in hauling the sledge $24\text{ m}$.

questions.prompt:
A mining truck of mass $800\text{ kg}$ is hauled from rest at the bottom of a slope of length $50\text{ m}$ inclined at $16^\circ$ to the horizontal. A constant resistance of $250\text{ N}$ opposes motion at all times. The haulage occurs in two stages:
- Stage 1: The truck accelerates uniformly from rest over the first $20\text{ m}$ with acceleration $0.6\text{ m s}^{-2}$ under a constant pulling force $P_1$.
- Stage 2: The truck continues for the remaining $30\text{ m}$ to the top of the slope at the constant speed achieved at the end of Stage 1 under a constant pulling force $P_2$.
The pulling force acts parallel to the line of greatest slope throughout. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: For Stage 1, find the speed of the truck at the end of the $20\text{ m}$, calculate the magnitude of the pulling force $P_1$, and determine the work done by $P_1$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For Stage 2, calculate the pulling force $P_2$, the work done by $P_2$, and verify the work-energy balance across the entire $50\text{ m}$ journey by comparing total work done by the pulling forces with the sum of gravitational potential energy gained, kinetic energy gained, and total work done against resistance.

questions.prompt: A cable car of mass $1200\text{ kg}$ is being lowered down a steep mountainside track inclined at $35^\circ$ to the horizontal. A winch cable attached to the car exerts a restraining tension $T$ acting parallel to and up the line of greatest slope. A constant track resistance of $800\text{ N}$ opposes the downward motion of the car. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: If the cable car descends a distance of $45\text{ m}$ at a constant speed of $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$, calculate the tension $T$ in the cable, and find the work done by the tension force during this descent.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The winch operator now increases the cable tension to $T_{\text{brake}} = 8500\text{ N}$ to bring the car to rest from its speed of $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the deceleration of the car during this braking phase, and calculate the distance travelled and the work done by gravity while coming to rest.
